# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 70 (Bu-Vb Pc70)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc70  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 70  
**Title (English, from literature):** Supporting a novice monk with a bad view  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 70 is the tenth and concluding training rule of the *Sappāṇavagga* in the Pātimokkha [Vinayamukha 1983]. The rule proscribes associating with, sheltering, eating with, or being served by a novice (*sāmaṇera*) who has been expelled from the community for clinging to the false view that things declared obstructive (*antarāyika*) by the Buddha are not genuinely obstructive [Wijayaratna 1990; Vinayamukha 1983]. According to the origin narrative, the novice Kaṇḍaka maintained this distorted teaching and refused to relinquish it after being admonished three times [Wijayaratna 1990; Vinayamukha 1983]. Consequently, the Sangha enacted expulsion (*nāsanā* or *nissāranā*) by a formal act of authorization (*apalokanakamma*), barring him from calling the Buddha his teacher and expelling him from the residence; should the expelled novice later acknowledge the fault, he can be reinstated (*osāretabbo*) via another *apalokanakamma* [Wijayaratna 1990; Vinayamukha 1983; Hüsken 1997].
